executiveSummary.title: WHAT THE DATA SAYS
executiveSummary.narrative:
Hilton New York Times Square appeared in at least one AI answer for 36.9% of the traveler needs we tested, and across every individual AI answer it appeared 23.1% of the time. Together, these results show how broadly AI recognizes the hotel and how consistently a traveler would encounter it.

The clearest strength in this period is often placed near the top when ai ranks hotels. See the summary at left for the supporting numbers. Among AI answers where hotel ranking could be measured, Hilton New York Times Square appeared in the Top 3 62.5% of the time, showing how prominently it is positioned when AI includes it.

AI currently reflects 50% of the monitored facts and attributes that define the hotel, so important parts of the property proposition are not consistently represented in AI results. No comparable prior official monitoring period is available yet, so change over time is not shown.

sections.headline: Hilton New York Times Square's primary issue is entering AI consideration at all, especially for Meetings & Groups.
sections.keyInsight: AI Consideration is 23.1%, so the hotel appears in only a limited share of individual comparable responses. When the hotel is absent, New York Marriott Marquis repeatedly appears instead — a concentrated substitution pattern rather than a diffuse competitor list. Rank tactics have limited value until relevance improves. The binding constraint is becoming part of the answer set for the traveler needs the hotel currently misses.
sections.whyItMatters: Fine-tuning rank against individual competitors will have limited value until the hotel becomes relevant in more of the traveler needs it currently misses. Entry problems and rank problems require different management attention. If leadership optimizes competitor comparisons first, the hotel can look busy while still missing the larger answer-set gap.
sections.focusNow: Focus first on how the hotel is represented for Meetings & Groups. Review whether the attributes, positioning, and use cases most relevant to those travelers are complete and consistently represented across priority sources. Treat competitor-rank tactics as secondary until entry improves.
sections.whatToReview: Compare evidence from scenarios where New York Marriott Marquis appears with the property information currently available for Hilton New York Times Square. Check entry cues first — product type, occasion, and location framing — before broadening the review to secondary attributes.
